stem.text: A potentiometer circuit is used to determine the electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E_\text{X}$ of a cell. The circuit includes a second cell of known e.m.f. $E_\text{0}$ and negligible internal resistance, and a uniform resistance wire PQ of known length.
The movable connection J can be positioned anywhere along the length of the resistance wire.
Which circuit is suitable for determining $E_\text{X}$?

A.alt: Potentiometer circuit with wire PQ. Cell labelled E0 in the upper wire, cell labelled EX on the lower left, a galvanometer, and a sliding contact labelled J on the wire.

B.alt: Potentiometer circuit with wire PQ. Cell labelled EX in the upper wire, galvanometer and cell labelled E0 in the lower branch, and a sliding contact labelled J on the wire.

C.alt: Potentiometer circuit with wire PQ. Galvanometer in the upper branch, cell labelled E0 on the upper right, cell labelled EX at the bottom left, and a sliding contact labelled J on the wire.

D.alt: Potentiometer circuit with wire PQ. Cell labelled EX on the upper left, galvanometer above the wire, cell labelled E0 at the bottom, and a sliding contact labelled J on the wire.
